description: Draft contracts this build can read ONLY through the explicitly requested rule-V7 lane. These are not released contracts: neither type has a row in the shared schemas/versions.json, a published schemaVersion of its own, a w3id URL or a release tag, and nothing in this file changes that. Each entry pins the exact bytes of one draft file by the commit of the development repository that owns the type and the SHA-256 of those bytes, which is how docs/SCHEMA-VERSIONS.md V7 requires a draft to be read: selection runs against the pinned bytes, never against a repository's main at run time. Two revisions are pinned per type and they are different things: `commit` is the revision of the contract bytes this library compiles and validates against, and `suiteCommit` is the revision of the owning repository's development conformance suite whose manifest `scripts/draft_vectors.jl` executes. They are separate keys because the two files move at different times, and because the suite carries the rule labels this file quotes: a claim about C1/C2/C3 or K1-K6 is a claim about the suite revision, never about the contract revision. Where they are equal, `suiteCommit` repeats `commit` so the check is uniform. `src/drafts.jl` re-verifies every digest the first time a draft is loaded and refuses to read on a mismatch; `test/runtests.jl` calls `verify_draft_bytes()` on every test run, and `check_suite_pin()` is the guard the draft runner refuses to score without. The lane is never the default: with no explicit user decision these files are not read at all and a draft citation is 'any other value' under V5, exactly as it was before the lane existed. This registry is deliberately separate from schemas/provenance.json, which lists released contracts only and stays that way.
rule: docs/SCHEMA-VERSIONS.md rule V7 (FAIR-bioHeaders-Specification#221/#226, text published at tag v0.6.0)

scheduledPublication.note: A scheduled future release is a decision about that type, not a licence to publish it here. Until the release lands these entries stay drafts: no schemaVersion claim, no fixed alias, no registry row, no support claim.

FHT.note: An FHT header is a FASTA `;~` block like FHR, so it shares the FASTA container; the type is decided by the record's own `schema` citation. Its conformance rules are C1 (contract validation), C2 (schema-URL closure) and C3 (parent-link verification) - text in the FHT-Specification conformance README. C2 is inside the pinned bytes; C3 is judged by the draft-lane runner in scripts/draft_vectors.jl, which recomputes a supplied parent's checksum and reports checked-pass / checked-fail / unchecked per derivedFrom entry. C3 is not claimed for the released types.

This changes no released schema, contract identity or V7 default. Historical prior overlay and digest remain recorded in parent cfbab3d8; this dated refresh makes no contract adoption claim.

FHGM.note: FHGM is not a file header type: an FHGM record carries no `schema`, no `schemaVersion` and no `checksum`. Records ride inside an FHGFF3 header under the R15 extension key `x-fhgm-models`, the file keeps its released FHGFF3 citation and is routed by V1 to V3, and the file checksum covers every record byte (R3). The V7 lane therefore selects only the contract applied to the records; a file citing the FHGM contract URL as its `schema` is 'any other value' under V5, with the lane open or shut. Model-level rules K1-K6 and the boundary B1 are drafted in FHGM-Specification; src/fhgm.jl implements K1, K2, K3, K5 and K6 and reports K4 (feature-target resolution) as not-supported-yet, because resolving a featureId needs the GFF3 feature layer, which this library's boundary assigns to gff3-validator.
